questions.prompt: What is Odin's implicit `context` parameter?

options.text: A global mutable singleton shared across all threads
A hidden per-call-stack struct passed to Odin procedures containing `allocator`, `temp_allocator`, `logger`, and `user_ptr`

questions.prompt: How do you temporarily override `context.allocator` for a block without affecting the caller?

options.text: Assign `context.allocator = arena_alloc` inside a new scope (optionally using `context = context` or `defer`)
It cannot be changed at runtime

questions.prompt: What is `context.temp_allocator` designed for?

options.text: Long-lived application state that persists until exit
Short-lived scratch allocations (e.g., per-frame or per-request) freed all at once via `free_all(context.temp_allocator)`

questions.prompt: How does `mem.Tracking_Allocator` help during development and testing?

options.text: It compresses heap allocations with LZ4
It records allocations and frees so you can detect memory leaks and double/bad frees
It pins pages in kernel memory

questions.prompt: Select all valid statements about Odin's allocator model. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: An `Arena` allocator can free all its allocations in O(1) via `free_all`
Odin's `mem.Allocator` is a struct of `(procedure, data)` so custom allocators plug in uniformly
Individual `free()` calls are required on a linear arena before resetting it
`make`, `new`, and `append` use `context.allocator` by default unless given another allocator

questions.prompt: Match each allocator or pattern to its best engineering use case.

columns.label: Per-frame or per-request scratch strings and buffers
Phase-scoped objects freed together in one call

questions.prompt: Why can Struct-of-Arrays (`#soa`) outperform Array-of-Structs (AoS) in tight loops?

options.text: `#soa` moves all data into CPU registers permanently
`#soa` stores each field contiguously, improving CPU cache line utilization and SIMD vectorization when only a subset of fields is accessed

questions.prompt: What does `#soa[100]Entity` or `#soa[]Entity` do in Odin?

options.text: Transforms the layout into Struct-of-Arrays while letting you index `entities[i].pos`
Declares a normal AoS array sorted by name

questions.prompt: What are `soa_zip` and `soa_unzip` used for in Odin?

options.text: Pairing separate slices into a virtual `#soa` slice (`soa_zip`) and extracting field slices back out (`soa_unzip`)

questions.prompt: What is a key difference between `when` and `if` regarding dead code and type checking?

options.text: `when` branches are both fully type-checked even if false
An untaken `when` branch is not semantically checked for type errors or missing OS-specific symbols

questions.prompt: How do you restrict an `.odin` source file to compile only on Linux?

options.text: `#+build linux` at the top of the file

questions.prompt: What does `foreign import lib "system:m"` declare?

options.text: Links an external native library (such as C's math library `libm`) for `foreign` declarations
Imports an Odin package from GitHub
Creates a dynamic plugin at runtime

questions.prompt: Why must Odin C FFI procedures typically use `proc "c"` and `cstring`?

options.text: `proc "c"` matches the C ABI (no implicit Odin `context`), and `cstring` is a null-terminated `^u8` expected by C
Odin's `string` is already null-terminated in all cases

questions.prompt: What does `@(link_name="custom_sym")` on a `foreign` procedure do?

options.text: Inlines the C function into Odin
Maps an Odin procedure identifier to a different exported linker symbol name

questions.prompt: When writing a callback in Odin passed to a C library, what calling convention should you use?

options.text: `"c"` (which omits `context`, or initialize `context = runtime.default_context()` inside if needed)

questions.prompt: What happens to `context` when spawning a new thread with `core:thread`?

options.text: Each thread gets its own `context` (copied or initialized), and `thread.create` lets you provide `init_context`
The child thread shares the parent's `context` pointer unsafely
Odin forces all allocations onto `temp_allocator` globally

questions.prompt: Select all synchronization primitives provided in `core:sync` and `core:sync/chan`. (Select all that apply.)
How do you mark a procedure as a unit test discovered by `odin test`?
What does `testing.expect_value(t, got, expected)` do when `got != expected`?

options.text: Immediately aborts the OS process with `SIGABRT`
Records a test failure with both values and caller location without crashing other tests

questions.prompt: What happens in `odin test` if a `@(test)` procedure leaks memory allocated via `context.allocator`?

options.text: Leaks are automatically freed without warning
The default test runner wraps `context.allocator` with a `Tracking_Allocator` and reports leaks as test failures

questions.prompt: What does `thread.pool_init` / `thread.pool_add_task` in `core:thread` provide?

options.text: A fixed-size worker thread pool for executing queued tasks concurrently

questions.prompt: Why is `defer sync.mutex_unlock(&m)` preferred after `sync.mutex_lock(&m)`?

options.text: It unlocks the mutex on every exit path of the scope, preventing accidental deadlocks on early returns
It automatically upgrades the mutex to a read-write lock
It runs the unlock on a background thread

questions.prompt: Match each Odin attribute or directive to its effect.

columns.label: Eliminates padding bytes between struct fields
Disables bounds checking inside a procedure

questions.prompt: What does `-vet` do when passed to the Odin compiler?

options.text: Enables stricter warnings for unused variables, unused imports, shadowing, and style issues

questions.prompt: What is a common pitfall when returning a `string` formatted with `fmt.tprintf` from a function?

options.text: The returned string lives in `context.temp_allocator` and becomes invalid after `free_all(context.temp_allocator)`

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `strings.clone(s)`?

options.text: Allocates an independent copy of `s` using `context.allocator` (or a specified allocator)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Odin's `base:intrinsics` package. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Provides compile-time type queries like `type_is_numeric(T)` and `type_is_struct(T)`
Exposes low-level hardware operations like `count_leading_zeros` and atomic primitives

questions.prompt: What does `#simd[4]f32` represent in Odin?

options.text: A 4-lane hardware SIMD vector of `f32` supporting element-wise arithmetic

questions.prompt: What happens when you pass `-sanitize:address` to `odin build` or `odin run`?

options.text: Enables AddressSanitizer (ASan) to detect out-of-bounds accesses and use-after-free bugs at runtime

questions.prompt: Why should `free_all(context.temp_allocator)` be called at a clear boundary (like the end of a frame or request)?

options.text: Because Odin crashes if `temp_allocator` is not freed every millisecond
Because `temp_allocator` never wraps or resets on its own unless told to

questions.prompt: Select all practices that improve C FFI safety in Odin. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use `proc "c"` for foreign functions and callbacks
Pass Odin `[]u8` slices directly to C functions expecting `const char*` without a length
Use `strings.clone_to_cstring(s)` and `defer delete(cs)` when passing non-literal Odin strings to C
Verify struct field types and `#align` / `#packed` match the C ABI layout

questions.prompt: Match each `core:os` or `core:io` concept to its role.

columns.label: Reads a file into a newly allocated `[]u8`
Writes a `[]u8` buffer to a file path

questions.prompt: In `core:log`, what does `context.logger = log.create_console_logger()` enable?
What does `@(require_results)` on a procedure declaration enforce?

options.text: The procedure must return at least two values
Callers cannot silently discard the procedure's return value(s)
The procedure must be called at compile time

questions.prompt: What does `mem.zero_slice(buf)` or `runtime.mem_zero(ptr, size)` do?

options.text: Overwrites the memory region with zero bytes (useful for resetting buffers or clearing sensitive data)

questions.prompt: What is the effect of `-o:speed` vs `-debug` on runtime bounds checks?

options.text: `-o:speed` optimizes codegen while keeping bounds checks unless `-no-bounds-check` is explicitly passed

questions.prompt: How can a library procedure in Odin remain allocator-agnostic?

options.text: By accepting `allocator := context.allocator` as a default parameter

questions.prompt: Select all valid reasons to prefer an Arena allocator over individual `malloc`/`free` calls. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: All objects sharing a phase lifetime are freed in one `free_all` call
Eliminates per-object heap fragmentation within the arena
Allows freeing individual middle objects in O(1) while shrinking the arena
Allocation is a fast pointer bump

questions.prompt: What does `reflect.struct_fields_zipped(T)` in `core:reflect` allow at runtime?

options.text: Runtime inspection of a struct's field names, types, offsets, and struct tags using RTTI

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Data-Oriented Design in Odin. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Organizing hot data contiguously reduces CPU cache misses
`#soa` separates fields into parallel arrays while preserving indexed access syntax
`bit_set` packs boolean flags densely into machine words
Heap-allocated linked lists of polymorphic objects are preferred for inner loops

questions.prompt: Match each Odin compiler flag to its diagnostic or build role.

columns.label: Report unused variables, imports, and shadowing
Optimize compiled output for smaller binary size

questions.prompt: What is the recommended way to prevent a `defer delete(res)` bug when transferring ownership of a slice to a caller?

options.text: Return a pointer to a stack variable instead
Do not `defer delete(res)` on the success path—or only `defer` cleanup on error paths (`if err != nil`)
